subject: CuraHealth trial — environment decision pathway & success checklist
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika.shah@curahealth.com>, Ben Torres <ben.t@curahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: CuraHealth trial — environment decision pathway & success checklist

Hi Anika / Ben — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Call highlights (short):
- Objective: Evaluate Redwood to surface clinical insights from patient notes and enable a triage assistant prototype for clinicians.
- Key non-negotiables: PHI-safe handling, per-request audit logs, and end-to-end encryption.
- Performance baseline requested: p95 latency target, throughput target tied to 500 concurrent clinician sessions.

Recommended trial environments (proposal):
1) Hosted trial (fastest) — Redwood-managed, predictable onboarding, limited to de-identified datasets; no VPC. Good for quick feature validation and UI/UX evaluation.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity) — VNet peering optional, persistent GPU pool, better performance visibility and cost predictability. Good for scale & throughput testing.
3) VPC/private deployment (on-prem or cloud VPC) — required if PHI cannot leave CuraHealth environment; supports KMS/HSM and customer-managed audit trails. Longer lead time.

Success criteria (proposed) — we should agree on these for the POC:
- Quality: Clinician-facing triage suggestions match human raters >= 85% (as measured on the control prompt set).
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens); p50 <= 120ms.
- Throughput: sustain 500 concurrent sessions with median latency degradation < 20%.
- Security: KMS integration + audit-log streaming to your SIEM for all request/response events.
- Cost target: rough ballpark cost <= $X per 1M tokens (we’ll provide model-level estimates once dataset size is clear).

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Anika: confirm whether PHI will be allowed in Redwood-hosted trial or if VPC is required. That decision determines lead time and SOW.
- Ben: share a representative sample of prompts and expected request rate (anon or synthetic is fine).
- Marissa & Neha: please draft a technical runbook for each environment (hosted / dedicated / VPC) and a one-page SOW draft.
- Jonas: I’ll ask for a manager-level sign-off on accelerated capacity if they choose dedicated.

Attachments: preliminary SOW template + network requirements. I’ll open a HubSpot deal and a shared Drive folder (links below).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a proposed timeline after we hear back from Anika on PHI constraints.

— Rishi

Subject: RE: CuraHealth trial — environment decision pathway & success checklist

Thanks Rishi — adding a technical lens and a recommendation based on our constraints.

Quick notes:
- If PHI cannot exit CuraHealth’s environment, VPC/private deployment is the only compliant option. That typically requires a 4–6 week engineering window for network onboarding + KMS/HSM integration and cert review.
- For Dedicated sandbox we can offer reserved capacity with optional private peering; this reduces lead time to ~2 weeks if we can get firewall rules and a CIDR range from your networking team.
- Hosted trial is immediate (48–72h) but we’ll need a de-identified dataset and explicit written confirmation that no PHI is included.

Suggested evaluation matrix (attached as 'evaluation-matrix-template.xlsx'):
- Columns: success_metric, target_value, test_method, owner, pass/fail criteria, notes.
- Proposed owners: CuraHealth QA (quality tests), Redwood SE (latency/throughput), CuraHealth Security (compliance checks).

Network checklist (excerpt):
- Egress allowlist: 18.205.0.0/16 and 52.14.0.0/16 (example)
- TLS termination policy: mutual TLS optional for VPC
- Audit log sink: syslog/CloudWatch/Azure Monitor endpoint + retention policy

If Anika confirms PHI rule-of-thumb today, I’ll assemble a VPC-runbook and an estimate for the 4–6 week path. Otherwise we can stand up a hosted proof in 48–72h to validate prompts and baseline quality.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: CuraHealth trial — environment decision pathway & success checklist

Thanks Rishi and Marissa — good summary. Short answers from my side:
- PHI policy: For the initial evaluation we cannot send PHI to any third-party managed service. So hosted trial is out.
- Preferred route: Start with Dedicated sandbox with private peering if that gives us faster time-to-evaluate, and we’ll run synthetic/anonymized prompts in the hosted environment later for UI/UX checks.
- Key gating items we need before kick-off: SOC2 report, data retention policy, and confirmation of audit-log delivery method.

I’ll loop in networking (Ben) to share CIDR and firewall constraints this week. We’re aiming for an internal steering committee decision by May 28.

Anika
Director of Product, Clinical Data | CuraHealth

Good thread — two operational points from my side:

1) Capacity funding: If the customer selects Dedicated sandbox, we should offer a 30-day free pilot on reserved capacity (subject to approvals) to remove friction. Rishi — please include this as an optional line in the SOW draft.

2) Timeline accountability: we should publish a compact trial timeline with owners. Proposed (if Dedicated chosen):
   - Day 0–3: contract + network questionnaire complete (Anika / Ben / Rishi)
   - Day 4–10: infra onboarding (Marissa / Neha) — peering, firewall rules, KMS proof-of-concept
   - Day 11–17: baseline runs (quality + latency tests) and adjustments (Redwood SE + Cura QA)
   - Day 18–30: measurement window and final decision (Cura steering committee)

Please mark owners in the SOW and set a single point of contact on the Cura side for network questions so we don’t block. I’ll push the approvals for a 30-day sandbox credit once we have a signed SOW.

-Jonas
